mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in core inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals reduced inflation expectations, leading to lower real interest rates and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors shift to equities.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL declines for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that suppresses corporate borrowing and economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 24-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in the unemployment rate signals a tightening monetary policy during a strong labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic growth prospects.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE fails to predict SPX returns when the joint signal (FEDFUNDS up and UNRATE down) occurs, with 20-day returns being positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high labor market tightness regime (UNRATE below 4.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals strong labor demand, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE in this regime falls below 0.03 over any 18-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for residential construction, which correlates with higher economic activity and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1300.0 thousand units, it signals a weakening in the residential sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1300.0, or the Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 24-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO fails to predict negative SPX returns when both series decline, with 5-day returns being positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 100.0), a decline in manufacturing output signals reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy approaches a recession.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in this regime falls below 0.03 over any 18-month rolling window.
